newsitem.title: USA: CBOT SOYMEAL COLLAPSES ON WET WEATHER, OILS SLIPS.
newsitem.headline: CBOT SOYMEAL COLLAPSES ON WET WEATHER, OILS SLIPS.

text.p: CBOT soymeal futures collapsed Monday under the weight of forecasts for more rain across parched portions of the central U.S. Midwest, traders said.
Soyoil also closed lower but losses were trimmed late on a shortcovering rally ahead of Tuesday's USDA crop production and supply and demand report.

Weekend storms brought light rains to dry pockets of central Illinois and Indiana but forecasts called for another 0.50 to 1.50 inch with 60 percent coverage across Missouri, Illinois, Indiana and Ohio over the next 24 to 48 hours.
The market has been counting raindrops in recent weeks after an abnormally dry July left some pockets of central Illinois and Indiana in dire need of moisture, traders said.
August is considered the critical weather month for soybeans because deficient moisture during pod fill can cut yields, traders said.
As of Sunday, WSC said rainfall in Peoria over the last 30 days was 79 percent of normal. But in Indianapolis, the 30-day rainfall was 10 percent of normal.
Soymeal ended $9.70 to $4.40 lower, with December down $8.80 at $201.20 per ton. Soyoil settled 0.31 to 0.16 cent lower, with December down 0.25 cent at 22.11 cents a lb.

Trade was said to be thin ahead of Tuesday's USDA crop production and supply and demand reports. Analysts expected the crop production figure, the first survey-based estimate of the year, to show a record crop in the fields. But traders said the report will likely take a back seat to weather forecasts.

On the day, commercials were on both sides of the soyiol market but were said to be buyers late, pit sources said. ADM bought 200 lots each August and September soyoil and sold 100 December. Cargill Inc bought 400 September and 100 December and sold 100 September and 200 December.
FIMAT Futures bought 400 July and Smith Barney sold 400 December, pit sources said.
In soymeal, Continental Grain bought 200 August and 100 December while Central Soya bought 200 August and sold 100 each August and September.
FIMAT bought 300 December and Refco Inc sold 400 December, traders said.
Soymeal futures volume was estimated by CBOT at 12,000 lots, against Friday's 14,914. Soyoil volume was pegged at 7,000 lots, against Friday's 7,908.
